clue.text: Artist's joke representation of nude royals

parts.note: to josh is to tease or joke

indicators.note: a fresh representation of the letters of these words reorders them

explanation.surface: A painter's satirical picture of unclothed members of the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the artist to his wordplay. 'representation of' reworks NUDE ROYALS into UAREYNOLDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Joshua Reynolds was the great eighteenth-century English portrait painter and first president of the Royal Academy.

clue.text: Old German is maybe too short to take the lead in Griselda

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged some other way
the lead in a name is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A remark that someone is too small to play the title role in the opera Griselda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' shuffles TOO SHORT together with G, the first letter of Griselda.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ostrogoths were an eastern Germanic tribe of late antiquity, so one is an ancient Teuton.

clue.text: Henry V performance finally split into two parts

parts.note: Hal is the familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
taken as written

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A staging of Shakespeare's Henry V ends up divided into two halves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry V' reads as the play, but Henry gives HAL and the V stays as itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To halve something is to cut or divide it into two equal portions.

clue.text: Sailor isn't worried — he has strong drinks

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: worried letters are fretted into a new order

parts.note: the letters of the word without its apostrophe
he has contracts to he's

explanation.surface: A relaxed sailor reassures us while downing powerful liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges ISNT into SINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a potent green anise-flavoured spirit; the plural names several servings of it.

clue.text: Glitch deleting time from alarm

indicators.note: deleting signals that a letter is struck out of the word for alarm

parts.note: terror is extreme fear or alarm

explanation.surface: A technical fault where the time vanishes from an alarm clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deleting' strips T from TERROR.
explanation.definitionFit: A glitch is a fault or mistake, the kind of slip a computer reports.

clue.text: Folk singer in prison with a rapper

parts.note: nick is British slang for a prison or police station
Drake is a Canadian rapper

explanation.surface: A folk musician locked up alongside a hip-hop artist.
explanation.walkthrough: NICK is British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Drake was an English singer-songwriter of the late 1960s and early 1970s, known for folk albums like Pink Moon.

clue.text: Celebrate a legend of F1

parts.note: to laud is to praise or celebrate

explanation.surface: An invitation to honour a famous Formula One driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' looks like part of the definition but is the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Niki Lauda was an Austrian racing driver who won three Formula One world championships.

clue.text: Evil organisation quietly residing in secret complex

indicators.note: something residing in a place lives within it
complex means intricately tangled, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: P, piano, means quietly in music

explanation.surface: A villainous group operating discreetly from a hidden compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' rearranges SECRET into SECTRE, and 'residing in' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: SPECTRE is the criminal syndicate headed by Blofeld in the James Bond stories.

clue.text: Short-term workers receiving ordinary rates

indicators.note: receiving means the word for the workers takes something into it

parts.note: temps are temporary office staff

explanation.surface: Temporary staff being paid the standard hourly wage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rates' looks like pay, but means speeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempo is the speed or pace of something, especially music, so the plural means speeds.

clue.text: Praise former partner for leaving at first

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
to can mean for, as in a toast to someone

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Speaking well of an ex for being the first to walk out.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise enthusiastically.

clue.text: Adverse criticism is harsh and, from time to time, guarded

parts.note: strict and harsh both describe severe treatment

indicators.note: from time to time means only every other letter is kept

explanation.surface: Hostile reviews are severe and only occasionally restrained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from time to time' takes the even letters of guarded: U, R, E.
explanation.definitionFit: A stricture is a sharply critical remark or censure.

clue.text: Interminably insincere person introducing one new radio show?

indicators.note: interminably means without an end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a phoney is a fake, insincere person
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fake host presenting a fresh radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interminably' cuts PHONEY to PHONE, which is then followed by I and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone-in is a broadcast in which listeners call to speak on air; the question mark admits television has them too.

clue.text: A Democrat stops laughing and beaming

indicators.note: a thing that stops a gap is plugged into it

parts.note: riant is a literary word for laughing or smiling

explanation.surface: A US politician silences the laughter while grinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops' puts AD inside RIANT, a rare word for laughing.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiant can describe a face glowing with happiness, just like a broad smile.

clue.text: Novel's primary sources of satire concern one overseas pressman

indicators.note: primary sources are the first letters of each word that follows

explanation.surface: A description of a book's main ingredients: satire about a foreign correspondent.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. The clue also describes the book: Evelyn Waugh's Scoop satirises a journalist sent abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoop is Evelyn Waugh's 1938 comic novel about Fleet Street war reporting.

clue.text: Bird seen in region next to range of hills

indicators.note: next to places one piece directly beside the other

parts.note: a part is an area or region
a ridge is a long line of high ground

explanation.surface: A bird spotted in an area close to some hills.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a plump game bird of fields and moorland.

clue.text: Criminal has mostly pirated chart songs

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent out of order
mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A crook has illegally copied most of the popular music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims HAS to HA, and 'Criminal' rearranges HA with PIRATED.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit parade is a ranked list of the best-selling popular records.

clue.text: Head of television succeeds when acquiring top US drama

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter
acquiring means the word for succeeds takes something inside it

parts.note: to succeed is to win, so wins
a peak is a top or summit

explanation.surface: A TV chief wins by buying a hit American series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' looks like an adjective for the drama but is a noun giving PEAK, which 'acquiring' places inside the word for succeeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Twin Peaks is David Lynch's cult American television mystery series.

clue.text: I'm not sure I'm able to get into Australian instant coffee

indicators.note: to get into something is to go inside it

parts.note: a mo is a moment or instant
er is the hesitant noise of someone unsure
I can says I am able

explanation.surface: Someone doubtful whether they can slip into an Australian's instant coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instant' looks like a coffee type, but it is MO; ERICAN goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An americano is espresso diluted with hot water.

clue.text: Ashram is initially tidied up to welcome spiritual leader

indicators.note: tidied up means put into a new order
initially picks the first letter

parts.note: hi is a greeting or welcome

explanation.surface: A religious retreat gets cleaned up to receive its guru.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tidied up' rearranges ASHRAM plus I (from 'is initially') into MAHARIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharishi is a Hindu sage or guru, a title for a revered religious teacher.

clue.text: Weak type of cleaner conserving fancy silk

indicators.note: conserving means holding something within

parts.note: a mop is a cleaning tool

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A feeble sort of cleaning product that protects delicate silk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' turns SILK into ILKS, and 'conserving' puts it in MOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A milksop is a timid, feeble man lacking courage.

clue.text: Song of mourning, for instance, penned in a famous cathedral

indicators.note: penned in means enclosed, as livestock in a pen

parts.note: Ely in Cambridgeshire has a famous cathedral
eg, exempli gratia, means for instance

explanation.surface: A lament heard within the walls of a great cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is an English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a poem or song lamenting the dead.

clue.text: Bet made by sports pro in New York

definitions.meaning: a multiple wager of eleven bets on four selections
a player for the New York baseball team

explanation.surface: A wager placed by a New York athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: A yankee is a bookmaker's term for a combination bet.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York Yankees baseball club gives its players this name, and bookmakers use it for a four-selection accumulator.

clue.text: Progressive artist involved in false reporting

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside

parts.note: libel is a false published statement
RA, Royal Academician, is an artist

explanation.surface: A left-leaning painter caught up in a scandal about misleading news.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, for Royal Academician, is the standard crossword artist; 'involved in' places it inside the word for false reporting.
explanation.definitionFit: A liberal favours reform and progress in politics.

clue.text: I'm not impressed with this empty high street outlet

parts.note: boo is a cry of disapproval

indicators.note: empty removes the inside, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: A shopper unimpressed with a deserted store on the main street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves TS from 'this'. Boots is a British chain of chemist's shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Boots is a well-known British pharmacy chain found on most town high streets.

clue.text: Antisocial person left a certain party halfway through

parts.note: one can mean a certain, as in one Mr Smith

indicators.note: halfway through a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: An unsociable guest who walked out of a party midway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halfway through' picks R, the central letter of PARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A loner is someone who avoids company and prefers solitude.

clue.text: A Welsh lady's cat

parts.note: per means a, as in ten pence per item
Sian is a Welsh woman's name

explanation.surface: A pet belonging to a woman from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' gives PER, as in once a day = once per day.
explanation.definitionFit: The Persian is a long-haired breed of domestic cat.

clue.text: Short tunic from the bottom part of Morocco

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the bottom means reading upwards
short means cut off before the end

parts.note: a tabard is a sleeveless tunic

explanation.surface: A brief garment that comes from somewhere in southern Morocco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short tunic' looks like the definition, but 'Short' trims TABARD to TABAR, which 'from the bottom' reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabat is the capital city of Morocco.

clue.text: Small wood in an unkempt national park

indicators.note: unkempt means untidy, so the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: A little woodland inside an overgrown nature reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unkempt' rearranges WOODINAN into NOWDONIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowdonia (Eryri) is the mountainous national park in north Wales.

clue.text: Tone up, principally by running and callisthenic exercises

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, taking the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: Fitness advice: get fit mainly through jogging and gym work.
explanation.definitionFit: To brace is to tense or firm up the muscles, steadying the body.

clue.text: Remover of pathogens transferring parasites in and out

indicators.note: transferring moves things about, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Something that shifts parasites back and forth to get rid of germs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transferring' rearranges PARASITES, IN and OUT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasteurisation heats milk and other liquids to kill harmful bacteria.
